messages.author: b28a3b94cb6f8a9f
messages.subject: geom_errorbar with another dataset
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to plot errorbars and specify another dataframe to grab the
data (basically a kind of stat summary by hand).
I came to this point:


a <- data.frame(x=runif(10), y=rnorm(10), dy=rnorm(10)/10)
b <- data.frame(m=runif(10), n=rnorm(10), dn=rnorm(10)/10)

# this works fine
qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=y-dy, ymax=y+dy))
# this does not
qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_errorbar(aes(x=m, ymin=n-dn, ymax=n
+dn), data=b)
# while this does
qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_line(aes(x=m, y=n), data=b)


I'm convinced I missed something and I should probably specify the
data in another way. Please let me know.
Thank you in advance,

Thomas Julou

> qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_errorbar(aes(x=m, ymin=n-dn, ymax=n
> +dn), data=b)

The problem here (as the error message indicates) is that you have not
specified what variable should be mapped to the y axis in the call to
geom_errobar(). Since you do not specify, it defaults to y as
specified in the call to qplot(). But y does not exist in the
dataframe b!

Hope that helps,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: geom_errorbar with another dataset
parts:
Thanks! You're right…

qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_errorbar(aes(x=m, y=n, ymin=n-dn, ymax=n
+dn), data=b)
works perfectly!

But I find it rather confusing since y is not described as an
aesthetic in http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_errorbar.html
And I don't see why it's needed to draw an errorbar since there are
already ymin and ymax. (I'd have understood if it was something like y
and dy…)

Anyway, that does the job. I think it may be worth mentioning in the
help.
Best,

Thomas

On Jul 19, 6:18 am, thomas <thomas.ju...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks! You're right…
>
> qplot(x=x, y=y, data=a) + geom_errorbar(aes(x=m, y=n, ymin=n-dn, ymax=n
> +dn), data=b)
> works perfectly!
>
> But I find it rather confusing since y is not described as an

> And I don't see why it's needed to draw an errorbar since there are
> already ymin and ymax. (I'd have understood if it was something like y
> and dy…)

It is not geom_errorbar that is triggering the requirement for y. It
is that you listed a y aesthetic in your default list in the qplot
call, and so geom_errorbar is honoring that request, but can't find
the appropriate variable (also called y). If you use the ggplot()
syntax instead of the qplot() syntax, you can avoid setting a global
default y aesthetic:

ggplot() +
geom_point(aes(x=x,y=y), data=a) +
geom_errorbar(aes(x=m, ymin=n-dn, ymax=n+dn), data=b)

Note that I didn't need a "y=n" in the aesthetic list for
geom_errorbar. And this creates the same plot as Thomas' suggestion.
